{{short description|Turkish-American mathematician}}
'''Sema Salur''' is a Turkish-American mathematician, currently serving as a Professor of Mathematics at the [[University of Rochester]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Sema Salur |url=https://web.math.rochester.edu/people/faculty/salur/Sema_Salur_Home_Page/General_Information.html |website=University of Rochester}}</ref> She was awarded the [[Ruth I. Michler Memorial Prize]] for 2014–2015,<ref name=AWM>{{cite web |title=Ruth I. Michler Prize 2014-2015 |url=https://awm-math.org/awards/ruth-i-michler-prize/michler-prize-2014-2015/ |website=Association for Women in Mathematics}}</ref> a prize intended to give a recently promoted associate professor a year-long fellowship at [[Cornell University]];<ref>{{cite web |title=The Ruth I Michler Memorial Prize of the AWM |url=https://www-history.mcs.st-andrews.ac.uk/Honours/Michler_Memorial_Prize.html |website=St Andrews University}}</ref> and has been the recipient of a [[National Science Foundation]] Research Award beginning in 2017.<ref>{{cite web |title=Award Abstract #1711178: Manifolds with Special Holonomy and Applications |url=https://nsf.gov/awardsearch/showAward?AWD_ID=1711178 |website=[[National Science Foundation]]}}</ref> She specialises in the "geometry and topology of the moduli spaces of calibrated submanifolds inside [[Calabi–Yau manifold|Calabi–Yau]], [[G2 (mathematics)|G<sub>2</sub>]] and [[Spin(7)]] [[manifolds]]",<ref name=AWM /><ref name=ReceivesNSF>{{cite web |title=Professor Sema Salur receives NSF Research Award |url=https://web.math.rochester.edu/news-events/news/2017/02/ |website=University of Rochester}}</ref> which are important to certain aspects of [[string theory]] and [[M-theory]] in physics, theories that attempt to unite [[gravity]], [[electromagnetism]], and the [[strong nuclear force|strong]] and [[weak nuclear force]]s into one coherent [[Theory of Everything]].<ref name=ReceivesNSF />

==Education==
* 1993: B.S. in Mathematics, [[Boğaziçi University]], Turkey.<ref name=AWM />
* 2000: PhD in Mathematics, [[Michigan State University]]<ref name=AWM />
